result.name: read_encoded_pointer
result.declaration: unsafe fn read_encoded_pointer (reader : & mut DwarfReader , context : & EHContext < '_ > , encoding : u8 ,) -> Result < * const u8 , () >
result.documentation:
Reads a pointer from `reader` whose encoding is described by `encoding`.

 `encoding` must be a [DWARF Exception Header Encoding as described by the LSB spec][LSB-dwarf-ext].

 # Errors
 Returns `Err` if `encoding`
 * is not a valid DWARF Exception Header Encoding,
 * is `DW_EH_PE_omit`, or
 * combines `DW_EH_PE_absptr` or `DW_EH_PE_aligned` application part with an integer encoding
   (not `DW_EH_PE_absptr`) in the value format part.

 [LSB-dwarf-ext]: https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/LSB_5.0.0/LSB-Core-generic/LSB-Core-generic/dwarfext.html
rules: For safety, `encoding` must be a DWARF Exception Header Encoding as described by the LSB specification.

result.name: from_raw
result.documentation:
Constructs a `Thread` from a raw pointer.

 The raw pointer must have been previously returned
 by a call to [`Thread::into_raw`].

 # Safety

 This function is unsafe because improper use may lead
 to memory unsafety, even if the returned `Thread` is never
 accessed.

 Creating a `Thread` from a pointer other than one returned
 from [`Thread::into_raw`] is **undefined behavior**.

 Calling this function twice on the same raw pointer can lead
 to a double-free if both `Thread` instances are dropped.
rules: The pointer passed to Thread::from_raw must have been previously returned by Thread::into_raw; passing any other pointer is undefined behavior, even if the returned Thread is never accessed.
If Thread::from_raw is called twice on the same raw pointer, the two resulting Thread instances must not both be dropped, as this can cause a double-free.
